Full Synopsis.value:
“This is a company that you will enjoy, fall in love with, and want to see again.”
– Ballet-Dance Magazine

 

“Sound and dance merge with one another; the body emancipates itself and becomes an instrument.”
– Stuttgarter Zeitung

 

“Exquisitely crafted, and worth seeing again and again.”
– Taipei Times

 

Internationally acclaimed and beloved worldwide, Cloud Gate Dance Theatre returns to Singapore with another stunning tapestry of movement, inspired by the sounds, shapes and fluidity of nature.

 

Created during the pandemic, Sounding Light begins from a renewed act of listening.

 

Inspired by the forest—its insects, birds, and the wind moving through trees—this work choreographed by Artistic Director Cheng Tsung-lung reflects on the shifting (im)balance between human civilisation and the natural world.

 

The choreography traces the passage of a single day. Sunlight moves, clouds gather, and shadows of leaves drift across space. Time is shaped through changing light, rhythm, and atmosphere.

 

Sound is created live on stage. The dancers become both movers and musicians, using breath, voice, finger snaps, and clapping in collaboration with composers Lim Giong and Chang Shiuan.

 

Movement and sound intertwine. Gestures echo birds and insects; bodies turn into instruments. Together, they evoke wind, rain, and flowing water—forming a world that is both seen and heard.

 

Premiered internationally at Kunstfest Weimar and HELLERAU – European Center for the Arts Dresden in 2024, the work has since been widely acclaimed and continues to tour internationally.

 

This programme is presented as part of da:ns focus – Connect Asia Now (CAN), a weekend that spotlights contemporary dance works created by or in collaboration with Asian artists, focusing on distinct voices and creative impulses from the region.

Full Synopsis.value:
Finally we're making it to the other side of the world to come play some music for you, can't wait. Been a long time but I have such nice memories of being there so I'll see you at the concert. – Patrick Watson

 

“Watson’s voice exists in that airy, impossible realm that seems more spiritual than physical in form” – Stereogum

“His repertoire is a supreme form of elegance, a silky setting from which a thousand images and a thousand feelings emerge,” – Les Inrocks

 

Patrick Watson composes, performs, and records his albums with his long-time bandmate and collaborator and multi-instrumentalists Mishka Stein and Olivier Fairfield. With more than 9.6 million monthly listeners on Spotify and over two billion global streams, this Canadian artist’s legacy extends across the globe, having reached Gold and Platinum status in multiple countries (including five certified gold albums in Canada) and thousands of sold out shows all over.

Over the course of his career, Patrick has retained the uncanny ability to coexist in mainstream pop-culture spaces and on the avant-garde fringes. Patrick’s songs have been featured in primetime crowd-pleasers like Grey’s Anatomy and This Is Us, as well as in multiple arthouse films from Denis Villeneuve (Polytechnique), Wim Wenders (Perfect Days), and Philippe Falardeau (C’est pas moi, je lejure!) and more. He’s an artist who’s as comfortable performing impromptu pop-up shows on the train tracks in a Quebec mining town as he is leading the BBC Orchestra at London’s prestigious Barbican. He’s an in-demand composer with over 15 film scores under his belt. He was awarded the prestigious inaugural Impact Award at the 2024 Canadian Sync Awards. Watson’s viral single Je te laisserai des mots became the first French song to accumulate 1 billion streams on Spotify.

Whether you discovered Patrick Watson through your local indie record shop, a movie soundtrack, a TikTok video a music festival, or his hit collaboration with Cinematic Orchestra (2007’s To Build a Home), his music has a similar effect on all who enter his kaleidoscopic sound-world. The songs of Patrick Watson transform your everyday surroundings into your own imaginary wonderland, translating stress and sorrow into joy, and helping you find peace within the chaos of modern life.

Popular Events.name: DOMi and JD BECK-WHO ASKED Tour
Popular Events.displayName: DOMi & JD BECK - WHO ASKED? Tour

Full Synopsis.value:
Widely regarded as two of jazz’s most innovative young artists, DOMi & JD BECK have redefined the genre with their fearless blend of intricate harmonies, breakneck rhythms, and playful internet-era sensibilities. The year they arrived on scene, they won over just about everyone: buttoned-up jazz fans, hip-hop heads, pop fans—you name it. Then, of course, came the GRAMMY Awards nominations for 2022’s NOT TiGHT, their debut record released by the iconic Blue Note Records in partnership with Anderson .Paak’s APESHIT, Inc. label. They were touted as the Gen Z ambassadors for jazz... up until they seemingly vanished.

What happened? Well, the answer comes in the form of their sophomore album, WHO ASKED?

Somehow both simpler and more complex than their debut, this album was two years in the making, born entirely from the duo’s home studio in Dallas, Texas. “This time around we felt like we had a pretty sharp idea of what we wanted the album to be before even starting,” say DOMi & JD BECK. “We wanted it orchestral, fully written out before even playing one note, with stronger songwriting intentions but just as crazy playing-wise and harmony-wise. We just wanted every note to mean something, and nothing left to chance.”

There are no big features on the album save for a small sinfonietta of seasoned classical players. What you hear—literally, as their voices also feature in their music for the first time—is all DOMi and JD BECK. You could almost call it chamber pop, if you multiplied the notes and destabilised the time signatures. Indietronica rooted in jazz with flourishes of hippie, flower-child freedom.

Turns out, their disappearance was not much of one, after all. They were just locked in, as they always are, to the music. Going back on the road, here’s a chance for fans to encounter this duo’s brilliance live in technicolour once again, no holds barred.

Page Description.value: New-gen jazz whizzkids DOMi & JD BECK return with more madcap rhythms, irreverent melodies and virtuosic improvisations.

Full Synopsis.value:
Join Jeremy Monteiro and an extraordinary cast of friends for a sizzling, soulful and virtuosic celebration of 50 years in jazz!

Marking five decades since he began his professional career in 1976, Jeremy brings together a stellar international ensemble featuring celebrated French trumpeter and co-founder of the Paris Jazz Big Band, Nicolas Folmer; Singapore saxophonist Sean Hong Wei, the enfant terrible of the Singapore jazz scene; and one of Asia’s finest jazz guitarists, Eugene Pao.

They are joined by the formidable rhythm section of Ben Poh on bass and Hong Chanutr Techatananan on drums, along with the astonishing young vocalist Maya Raisha, currently pursuing her Master’s degree in Jazz Studies in New York as a scholar of Jazz Association (Singapore).

Fifty years after first stepping onto the professional stage, Jeremy Monteiro is still swinging, still searching, and still making music with joy, fire and heart. This evening will feature favourite jazz standards, beloved original compositions, new works, and tender ballads—music that reflects a lifetime of friendship, swing, soul and artistic adventure.

Items.name: Dee Dee Bridgewater Duo with Helen Sung
Items.displayName: Dee Dee Bridgewater Duo with Helen Sung

Full Synopsis.value:
A fearless voyager, explorer, pioneer and keeper of tradition, Dee Dee Bridgewater has ascended to the upper echelon of vocalists over the course of a multifaceted career spanning four decades. This jazz giant and multiple GRAMMY and Tony Award-winner has become well known for taking intrepid leaps of faith in re-envisioning jazz classics, parsing cuts from The Great American Songbook through her own singular artistic vision.

She earned her first professional experience with the legendary Thad Jones/Mel Lewis Big Band, and then went on to share stages with jazz greats throughout the ‘70s, including Sonny Rollins and Dizzy Gillespie. In the ‘90s, she began producing her own work resulting in a string of influential records: 1993’s Keeping Tradition, 1997’s tribute to the late Ella Fitzgerald, Dear Ella, 1997’s Love And Peace: A Tribute To Horace Silver. Into the 2000s, she released the GRAMMY award-winning Eleanora Fagan (1915-1959): To Billie With Love From Dee Dee Bridgewater, before exploring other musical and spiritual roots in 2015’s Dee Dee’s Feathers and 2017’s Memphis… I’m Ready. 2025 brought the release of Elemental, the GRAMMY Award-nominated studio recording of Bridgewater’s collaboration with pianist Bill Charlap.

With film, television, Broadway, radio broadcasting and soundtrack credits, Bridgewater is an accomplished entertainment “polymath.” As she flourished in music, so did she in theatre, winning a Tony Award for her role as Glinda in the 1975 production of The Wiz. She continued garnering praise and acclaim for stage productions such as Lady Day, Sophisticated Ladies, Black Ballad, Carmen, Cabaret, among others. She also served as the namesake host of the long-running syndicated NPR radio program JazzSet with Dee Dee Bridgewater. Off-stage, Bridgewater is equally accomplished: she is an NEA Jazz Master, Doris Duke Artist, Memphis Music Hall of Fame inductee, and global Goodwill Ambassador to the United Nations.

Returning to Singapore after more than a decade, Bridgewater promises an intimate performance with her counterpart, pianist Helen Sung—a 2021 Guggenheim Fellow and graduate of the Thelonious Monk Institute of Jazz Performance—in one evening filled with sheer virtuosity and pure charm.

Full Synopsis.value:
Part performance, part living sculpture, Still Lives transforms a fleeting moment into a shared space for reflection, revealing how personal memories, social relationships and cultural histories become entangled. Presented previously in cities such as Venice, Melbourne and Glasgow, Still Lives now arrives in Singapore.

As a special edition developed with Esplanade – Theatres on the Bay, Still Lives: Singapore features RUDRA, Singapore’s pioneering Vedic metal band, whose journey ran alongside the nation’s rapid economic and cultural transformation since the 1990s.

Members and instruments of RUDRA are bound and suspended within intricate rope structures in the Singtel Waterfront Theatre at Esplanade, creating a visually arresting landscape through which audiences can reflect on the stories that shape Singapore’s cultural identity—particularly those that have existed beyond the mainstream.

This programme is presented as part of da:ns focus – Connect Asia Now (CAN), a weekend that spotlights contemporary dance works created by or in collaboration with Asian artists, focusing on distinct voices and creative impulses from the region.

 

Production credits
Lead Artists: Daniel Kok and Luke George
Collaborator: RUDRA
Sound Designer and Performer: Marco Cher-Gibard
Lighting Designer: Katie Sfetkidis
Representation and Distribution: Something Great

 

Recipient of two 2022 Green Room Awards (Melbourne) - Contemporary & Experimental Performance: Outstanding Achievement + Design & Technical Achievement

This evening will feature favourite jazz standards, beloved original compositions, new works, and tender ballads—music that reflects a lifetime of friendship, swing, soul and artistic adventure.

Full Synopsis.value:
A fearless voyager, explorer, pioneer and keeper of tradition, Dee Dee Bridgewater has ascended to the upper echelon of vocalists over the course of a multifaceted career spanning four decades. This jazz giant and multiple GRAMMY and Tony Award-winner has become well known for taking intrepid leaps of faith in re-envisioning jazz classics, parsing cuts from The Great American Songbook through her own singular artistic vision.

She earned her first professional experience with the legendary Thad Jones/Mel Lewis Big Band, and then went on to share stages with jazz greats throughout the ‘70s, including Sonny Rollins and Dizzy Gillespie. In the ‘90s, she began producing her own work resulting in a string of influential records: 1993’s Keeping Tradition, 1997’s tribute to the late Ella Fitzgerald, Dear Ella, 1997’s Love And Peace: A Tribute To Horace Silver. Into the 2000s, she released the GRAMMY award-winning Eleanora Fagan (1915-1959): To Billie With Love From Dee Dee Bridgewater, before exploring other musical and spiritual roots in 2015’s Dee Dee’s Feathers and 2017’s Memphis… I’m Ready. 2025 brought the release of Elemental, the GRAMMY Award-nominated studio recording of Bridgewater’s collaboration with pianist Bill Charlap.

With film, television, Broadway, radio broadcasting and soundtrack credits, Bridgewater is an accomplished entertainment “polymath.” As she flourished in music, so did she in theatre, winning a Tony Award for her role as Glinda in the 1975 production of The Wiz. She continued garnering praise and acclaim for stage productions such as Lady Day, Sophisticated Ladies, Black Ballad, Carmen, Cabaret, among others. She also served as the namesake host of the long-running syndicated NPR radio program JazzSet with Dee Dee Bridgewater. Off-stage, Bridgewater is equally accomplished: she is an NEA Jazz Master, Doris Duke Artist, Memphis Music Hall of Fame inductee, and global Goodwill Ambassador to the United Nations.

Returning to Singapore after more than a decade, Bridgewater promises an intimate performance with her counterpart, pianist Helen Sung—a 2021 Guggenheim Fellow and graduate of the Thelonious Monk Institute of Jazz Performance—in one evening filled with sheer virtuosity and pure charm.

Full Synopsis.value:
Part performance, part living sculpture, Still Lives transforms a fleeting moment into a shared space for reflection, revealing how personal memories, social relationships and cultural histories become entangled. Presented previously in cities such as Venice, Melbourne and Glasgow, Still Lives now arrives in Singapore.

As a special edition developed with Esplanade – Theatres on the Bay, Still Lives: Singapore features RUDRA, Singapore’s pioneering Vedic metal band, whose journey ran alongside the nation’s rapid economic and cultural transformation since the 1990s.

Members and instruments of RUDRA are bound and suspended within intricate rope structures in the Singtel Waterfront Theatre at Esplanade, creating a visually arresting landscape through which audiences can reflect on the stories that shape Singapore’s cultural identity—particularly those that have existed beyond the mainstream.

This programme is presented as part of da:ns focus – Connect Asia Now (CAN), a weekend that spotlights contemporary dance works created by or in collaboration with Asian artists, focusing on distinct voices and creative impulses from the region.
